scope: Retention configuration and temporary-record cleanup only; document/file expiry and full M4 acceptance remain open
verifiedBehavior: Configured retention periods load from YAML, reject invalid values and update without restart.
Expired open proposals become expired and emit a retained conversation event; executing proposals are preserved.
Resolved proposal metadata is pruned after its configured lifetime, while saved conversation payloads remain live.
A released payload with no remaining owner is removed without an additional age delay; detached never-owned payloads have a configured grace period.
Generic payload refs, direct foreign keys and prepared/applied mutation plans protect referenced bodies, including unknown referrer kinds.
Expired API idempotency entries and old retrieval traces are pruned in bounded batches; fresh entries remain.
Metadata cleanup is available through an admin endpoint, requires step-up for sessions and revalidates actor authority in the writer.
The hourly background run was exercised with controlled time against real repositories and only removed the expired orphan.
scheduler: Starts after one hour, drains at most 16 bounded batches per cycle, retries backlog or transient database failures after one minute.
notes: The first build exposed a store callback signature mismatch, corrected before functional tests.
The initial targeted API run passed the behavior check and found the expected composition/OpenAPI golden differences. The additions were reviewed and the snapshots updated.
The final regression includes the last-owner release rule and the scheduled-cleanup test.
limitations: This endpoint and worker cover temporary records. Trash purge, removed-document/identity expiry, debug-log files, backup rotation and the aggregate maintenance operation are still required.
The retention configuration includes the eventual document/file policy fields; those fields do not yet drive document or file deletion.
No new retention browser UI or CLI command is claimed by this checkpoint.
Large-corpus retention latency has not been qualified. Row mutation batches are bounded, but that alone does not prove the latency bound.
Remaining enrichment/provider/budget, backup/restore/export, release supply-chain, production migration and hardened deployment gates remain open.
No production service or user data was changed.
